source_text:
Ἀκηδία, φιλία ἀερικὴ, βημάτων περιαγωγὸς, φιλεργίας μῖσος, ἡσυχίας μάχη, ψαλμῳδίας ζάλη, εὐχῆς ὄκνος, ἀσκήσεως χαύνωσις, ἄωρος
νυσταγμὸς, περιστρεφόμενος ὕπνος, μανίας βάρος, κέλλης μῖσος, πόνων ἀντίπαλος, καρτερίας ἀντίζυγος, μελέτης κήμωτρον, Γραφῶν ἀμαθία, λύπης μέτοχος, ὁρωλόγιον πείνης. Ὑπομονὴ, ἀκηδίας διακοπὴ, λογισμῶν κατακοπὴ, θανάτου μέριμνα, σταυροῦ μελέτη, καθηλωμένος φόβος, τυπτόμενος χρυσὸς, θλίψεων νομοθήκη, βίβλος εὐχαριστίας, θώραξ ἡσυχίας, πόνων ὅπλον, ἀναζέουσα καλλιπονία, ἀρετῶν ὑπογραφή. Κενοδοξία, συντυχίας φαντασία, σχημάτισμα φιλοπονίας, ἀληθείας ἐναντία, αἱρέσεων ἀρχηγέτις, ὄρεξις προεδρίας, ἐσχάτη προσηγορίας, ἐπαίνων δουλεία, πολυσχημάτιστον πνεῦμα, μυριόδοντον θηρίον, κενοδοξίας μέση ὑπερηφανίᾳ πέπλεκται καὶ φθόνῳ, ἐν ἀλλήλοις ὄντα, καὶ δι' ἀλλήλων πολεμοῦντα, ἡ τρίσυρος ἅλυσις τῶν κακῶν, τὸ τριφάρμακον κέρασμα τῶν παθῶν, ἡ τριττὴ γλῶττα τῶν αἱρετικῶν. Ἀκενοδοξία, ταπεινοφροσύνης ἐργασία, ἀρεσκείας ἀποστασία, ἐπαίνων ἀβλεψία, γνώσεως θεωρία, κόσμου ἐναντία, ψυχῆς εὐαισθησία, εὐτελείας δόγμα, πόνων κρυπτηρία, εὐφημίας πολεμία, ἐν φθαρτῷ σώματι ἀπόκρυφος θησαυρός. Φθόνος, ὑπερηφανίας ἔνδυμα, ταπεινοφροσύνης ἀπόδυμα, καταλαλιᾶς ῥίζα, εὐθυμίας ὀφθαλμία, φιλίας ὑπόκρισις, παῤῥησίας δόλος, ἀγάπης ἔχθρα, εὐδοκιμούντων ζῆλος, εὐσταθούντων τύρβη, εὐφημουμένων σκῶμμα, ὀφθαλμῶν ἀλλοίωμα. Τίς ἐστιν ὁ καθαρὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὁ μὴ λαμβανόμενος ἑαυτοῦ ἐπὶ ἐντολῆς Θεοῦ ἀθετήσει, ἢ ἐλλείψει, ἢ ἐν ἀμελείᾳ; Χριστὸς δὲ ἡμῶν ἔστω παντὶ ἔργῳ θελήματος αὐτοῦ εὔοδος. Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν. 2
thought_title: Listlessness, endurance, vainglory, freedom from vainglory, envy, and the closing prayer
orientation: Evagrius finishes his list of the eight vices and their opposing virtues and then closes the work with a question and prayer.
pass_a_gloss: Listlessness is airy friendship, a leading about of steps, hatred of love for work, war against stillness, vertigo of psalm singing, shrinking from prayer, slackening of ascetic training, untimely nodding in sleep, sleep tossing to and fro, weight of madness, hatred of cell, adversary of labors, weight set against endurance, muzzle of meditation, ignorance of Scriptures, sharer in grief, timepiece of hunger. Endurance is cutting off of listlessness, cutting down of thoughts, care of death, meditation on the cross, fear nailed fast, gold under beating, law code of afflictions, book of thanksgiving, breastplate of stillness, weapon of labors, toil for the good boiling up, outline of virtues. Vainglory is imagining of a meeting, putting on the shape of love for toil, adversary to truth, foundress of heresies, desire for first seats, extremity of being addressed by title, slavery to praises, spirit of many forms, wild beast with countless teeth; in the middle of vainglory it has been plaited together with pride and with envy, being things in one another and making war through one another, the chain of evils dragging in three ways, the cup of the passions mixed with three drugs, the triple tongue of the heretics. Freedom from vainglory is working of humility, desertion of pleasing men, not looking at praises, contemplation of knowledge, adversary to the world, sensitivity of soul, teaching of cheapness, hiding place of labors, adversary to fair speech, hidden treasure in a corruptible body. Envy is garment of pride, stripping off of humility, root of backbiting, disease of the eyes against cheerfulness, hypocrisy of friendship, deceit of frank speech, enmity of love, jealousy against those approved, confusion against those stable, mockery of those well spoken of, alteration of eyes. Who is the one pure in heart, who unless he takes hold of himself will annul the command of God, either by falling short or by neglect? But let our Christ be a prosperous way for every work of his will. To him be the glory into the ages. Amen.

choices.why: ἀερικὴ means airy or ethereal, describing the friendship as unreal and insubstantial
ὡρολόγιον is a timepiece or clock; the phrase says listlessness tells time by hunger

choices.english: the chain of evils dragging in three ways
choices.why: τρίσυρος describes dragging in three directions, applied to the threefold chain of vainglory, pride and envy

choices.english: who unless he takes hold of himself
choices.why: middle participle with negative condition gives the force if he does not lay hold of himself
rejected: who is not apprehended of himself

pass_b_english: Listlessness is an airy friendship and a leading astray of footsteps. It hates hard work and battles stillness. It grows dizzy at psalm-singing and shrinks back from prayer. It slackens ascetic practice into untimely drowsiness and restless, turning sleep. It is a weight of madness and a hatred of the cell. It opposes labors and counterbalances perseverance. It muzzles meditation and leaves the Scriptures unlearned. It shares in grief and serves as a timepiece of hunger.

Endurance breaks off listlessness and cuts down thoughts. It keeps death in mind and meditates on the cross. It is fear nailed fast and gold under the hammer. It is a law book for afflictions and a book of thanksgiving. It is a breastplate for stillness and a weapon for labors. It is a fervent devotion to good work and a pattern for the virtues.

Vainglory is a fantasy of encounters and a pretense of hard work. It stands against the truth and leads the way for heresies. It hungers for the first seat and is last to offer a greeting. It is enslaved to praises, a spirit of many disguises, a beast with countless teeth. At its center vainglory is woven together with pride and envy, each living in the other and warring through the other. Together they are the chain of evils dragging in three ways, the draught of passions mixed with three poisons, and the threefold tongue of the heretics.

Freedom from vainglory is the working of humility. It breaks away from people-pleasing and pays no attention to praises. It contemplates knowledge and stands against the world. It gives the soul a keen sensitivity and teaches the doctrine of simplicity. It is a hiding place for labors and an enemy to reputation. It is a treasure hidden in a perishable body.

Envy is the clothing of pride and the stripping off of humility. It is the root of slander and a disease in the eye of cheerfulness. It counterfeits friendship and deceives with frankness. It hates love and burns against those who prove worthy. It unsettles those who stand firm and mocks those who are praised. It distorts the eyes. Who is pure in heart, who does not catch himself setting aside a commandment of God, or falling short, or in negligence? May our Christ prosper every work of his will. To him be glory forever. Amen.
notes: Trailing '2' after Amen in the source is a page or section number and is not translated.
ἐσχάτη προσηγορίας and the long question about the pure in heart are uncertain; glossed as written without supplying missing words.

problems.quote: who unless he takes hold of himself will break the commandment of God, or fall short, or drift in negligence?
problems.source_quote: ὁ μὴ λαμβανόμενος ἑαυτοῦ ἐπὶ ἐντολῆς Θεοῦ ἀθετήσει, ἢ ἐλλείψει, ἢ ἐν ἀμελείᾳ;
problems.why: Misreads dative nouns ἀθετήσει and ἐλλείψει (with ἐπὶ) as future verbs and ὁ μὴ λαμβανόμενος ἑαυτοῦ ('who does not catch himself') as a conditional, garbling the sense.
problems.fix: who does not catch himself setting aside a commandment of God, or falling short, or in negligence?

problems.why: συντυχία means 'meeting, encounter, conversation' (or 'chance'), not 'worldly success'; the English confuses it with εὐτυχία and adds 'worldly'.
problems.fix: a fantasy of encounters and conversations

problems.quote: and for the final word of greeting.
problems.why: ἐσχάτη is nominative agreeing with vainglory, not governed by ὄρεξις; 'final word of greeting' misreads the syntax and makes no sense for 'last to greet'.
problems.fix: and is last to offer a greeting.

edits.old: and for the final word of greeting.
edits.new: and is last to offer a greeting.

edits.old: who unless he takes hold of himself will break the commandment of God, or fall short, or drift in negligence?
edits.new: who does not catch himself setting aside a commandment of God, or falling short, or in negligence?

fixed: fixed 'fantasy of worldly success' to 'fantasy of encounters': source συντυχίας φαντασία means imagining of meeting/encounter, not success.
fixed 'for the final word of greeting' to 'is last to offer a greeting': source ἐσχάτη is nominative agreeing with vainglory, not governed by ὄρεξις.
fixed conditional/future-verb reading to dative nouns: source ἀθετήσει, ἐλλείψει are datives of setting-aside/falling-short and ὁ μὴ λαμβανόμενος ἑαυτοῦ means not catching himself.
